source.title: Scaling Laws for Reranking in Information Retrieval
source.authors: Rahul Seetharaman; Aman Bansal; Hamed Zamani; Kaustubh D. Dhole

record.tranche_reason: Tests power-law scaling and forecasting in fine-tuned cross-encoder rerankers, a different training and evaluation setting from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling results for reranking metrics, chiefly NDCG@10, not held-out language-model pretraining loss. Its contrastive entropy (CE) is a secondary reranker diagnostic, not the pretraining cross-entropy named in the claim. The results bear on fine-tuning scaling and downstream performance predictability, but do not directly test the original pretraining-loss claim.
record.test_reason: It fits saturating power laws to reranking quality (NDCG@10, MAP, MRR, contrastive entropy) of fine-tuned Ettin cross-encoders over model size (17M–1B) and training exposure, and forecasts held-out 400M/1B models from runs up to 150M. This is a new fine-tuning setting with results on V5 (fine-tuning regime), V6 (downstream predictability) and V7 (dependence of the allocation and forecasts on objective and functional form). It does not measure language-model pretraining loss, so V1–V4 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that NDCG (and MAP) of cross-encoder rerankers follow predictable power laws over model size and training exposure. Runs up to 150M forecast 400M and 1B on MSMARCO-dev and TREC DL. MRR and CE are noisier. Fitted allocations favour data, but recommendations depend on the objective and should be checked with equal-compute runs. Their claim that forecasts are 'typically conservative' is not borne out by Table 8, where most point forecasts exceed the observed values.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fine-tuned cross-encoder rerankers and downstream ranking metrics (primarily NDCG@10), rather than language-model pretraining loss; studies pointwise, pairwise, and listwise objectives.
record.method_sensitivity: Objective changes fit quality, fitted compute-allocation exponents, and matched-compute outcomes. The additive joint law forecasts better than the tested multiplicative alternative.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched compute (C=N·D), 68M beats 400M for pointwise (0.319 vs 0.311) and pairwise (0.354 vs 0.342) NDCG@10. 400M beats 68M for listwise (0.351 vs 0.318), even though the fitted exponents favour data for all objectives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For fine-tuned rerankers, the metric-optimal split of compute between model size and training exposure depends on the objective, and fit-derived allocations can disagree with direct equal-compute comparisons.

record.code_released: The paper says code and evaluation protocols will be released; URL not stated.
record.problems: The experiments use one encoder-based cross-encoder family, fine-tuned for one epoch on 100K MS MARCO queries. The paper does not report BEIR results or test other model families, longer horizons, larger supervision sets, or curricula. Listwise model-scaling fit quality drops at 1B, and CE is less stable than NDCG. Bootstrap intervals are reported for selected forecasts, but not for the forecast-error values in the main table.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted separate MAP, MRR, Recall@10, P@10, CE, and TREC DL results, as well as the full per-size data-scaling tables (Tables 6-7 and 13-14). These additional results are described as broadly predictable for NDCG and MAP, while MRR and CE are noisier; they are not needed for the selected NDCG evidence. Table 6 is flattened in the supplied text, so individual cell-to-condition assignments were not inferred.

untested.parts: All of it: no language-model pretraining loss is measured.
Pretraining-loss extrapolation. The reranker forecasts extrapolate only about 7x in parameters (150M to 1B), not orders of magnitude.
All of it: no loss-minimising parameter/token split for pretraining. The reranker allocation results are recorded under fits_no_version.
All of it: one architecture family, with no shape variation at fixed size.
Other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, other reranker families, longer than one-epoch training, and extrapolation over orders of magnitude.
Predictability as a function of pretraining loss, other task families, and extrapolation beyond about 7x in size.
Parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, datasets, and the disagreement between published language-model laws.

missing.what: Joint-law final-checkpoint forecasts against observed values with bootstrap CIs. Coverage is 10 of 12; both misses are pointwise 400M. Most predictions sit above observed values (pointwise 400M: predicted 0.3742, observed 0.3519).

Contrastive-entropy (the reranker's loss-like measure) forecast errors, especially the pairwise breakdown: 400M RMSE 0.975, data-fit R² 0.12. Rows_left_out declares CE but understates it as 'noisier'; it should be rowed because it is the closest measure to a loss.
TREC DL model/data/joint forecast errors for NDCG, MAP and MRR (declared in rows_left_out). MRR is noticeably worse on TREC DL '19.

record.verdict_notes: This is a fine-tuning study of a single model family (Ettin, 17M–1B), with one epoch on about 100K MS MARCO queries. Extrapolation spans under one order of magnitude. Not one of the original sources. The reader's V7 label was changed from limits_scope to supports, because objective- and form-dependence is what V7 asserts. Table 1 and Table 13 disagree on the 150M data-scaling errors.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Forecasting held-out pretraining loss from smaller language-model pretraining runs; the forecasts here target reranking metrics.

Loss-minimising parameter and token counts for language-model pretraining. The study instead derives allocation exponents for reranking metrics and compares training exposure rather than token counts.
Architecture variation at fixed parameter count; the study uses one cross-encoder model family.
Other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, and transfer. The tested fine-tuning setting is cross-encoder reranking on MS MARCO.
Predictability of other downstream task families and predictability specifically as a function of pretraining loss.
Dependence on parameter-counting conventions, pretraining schedules, and other datasets or model families.
